name: Luxury sportswear

card.summary: Designer-priced athletic-inspired clothing, such as technical jackets, tracksuits and refined gym wear, used to look polished and put-together in casual settings.
card.aka: Luxury activewear, luxury athleisure, quiet luxury activewear

quick.overview:
Luxury sportswear is athletic-style clothing sold by designer or premium labels: tracksuits, performance-fabric jackets, leggings, joggers and knit pieces made with higher-end materials and tailoring. It helps looks through fit, fabric and a refined casual silhouette that reads as put-together outside the gym.

It grew out of athleisure, whose mainstream rise Wikipedia dates to the mid-2010s, and fashion media have followed designer entries into the category. A 2023 Equinox piece links the recent shift toward muted, logo-light gym wear to the quiet-luxury trend.
quick.how: People wear it as everyday clothing: a clean tracksuit or technical layer in place of jeans and a jacket, or elevated basics in neutral colours. Equinox's retail lead suggests judging seams, finishing and fabric feel.
quick.risks: The main downside is cost, and logo-heavy or ill-fitting pieces can read differently from the intended look. No health risks beyond ordinary clothing concerns such as sizing and fabric sensitivity.

lead: Luxury sportswear refers to athletic-inspired clothing priced and positioned as high fashion. It extends athleisure, the category of sportswear worn outside exercise, which Wikipedia says became recognised as a retail category in the mid-2010s [1].

In style terms it is used to look neat while staying casual: better fabrics, tailoring-informed cuts and restrained branding. An Equinox article from 2023 describes activewear moving toward muted, monochrome palettes, softer performance fabrics and less logo-driven design, which it ties to the quiet-luxury trend [2].

angle.text: Wearing well-cut, quality sportswear gives a tidy, intentional look in casual settings, and neutral colours and fit are used to flatter the frame.

paras: Wikipedia traces athleisure back to Champion hoodies in the 1930s, spandex in 1958 and Adidas tracksuits in the 1960s, with the modern trend establishing itself in the mid-2010s and growing through COVID-19 [1]. Reference lists in that article point to coverage of luxury entering the category, such as a Digiday piece on designer sneakers and expensive leggings [1].

Equinox's VP of Retail, Annie Walters, says the shift toward understated activewear has been building since 2021, favouring muted palettes, refined fabrics and fit over bold prints and logos [2]. She suggests checking seams, finishing and fabric hand, and notes that men are moving beyond black and navy and that shorter shorts are popular [2].

timeline.event: Athleisure becomes a recognised retail category, per Wikipedia [1].
Equinox describes quiet-luxury styling reaching activewear [2].
